top_cluster.headline: A wave of contested 2026 Democratic primaries — most notably Abdul El-Sayed's Michigan Senate win over Rep. Haley Stevens — has exposed a party rift between progressive/democratic-socialist candidates and the establishment, playing out alongside parallel primary fights in Wisconsin, Montana, Hawaii and South Carolina.
top_cluster.left_framing: Emphasizes party unity, reconciliation (El-Sayed consulting Obama), and populist economic contrasts with Trump's wealth; treats AOC's egg-freezing as an empowerment/reproductive-autonomy story tied to criticism of Trump-era health policy; largely avoids engaging with critiques of progressive candidates' specific liabilities.
top_cluster.center_framing: Treats the primaries analytically as strategic and electability contests: a 2028 proxy battle over Bernie-style populism (Axios), an internal ballot-access dilemma (NPR), and a referendum on Trump's personal influence and economic conditions rather than ideology (NPR).
top_cluster.right_framing: Frames Democratic primaries as evidence of party dysfunction and drift toward extremism — El-Sayed as a general-election liability, Hong as a dangerous socialist, Sanders exposing a 'corrupt system,' and establishment Democrats undemocratically pressuring Bankhead out — while casting AOC's announcement as politically motivated rather than personal.
top_cluster.left_omissions: Left coverage omits the Hasan Piker controversy and specific electability critiques of El-Sayed, the detailed radical policy specifics of Hong's platform, and the framing of establishment pressure on Bankhead as anti-democratic.
top_cluster.right_omissions: Right coverage omits the party-unity/reconciliation angle (Obama's involvement), the economic-headwinds-hurt-Republicans analysis, Trump's absence from the ballot as a midterm factor, and the reproductive-rights policy context behind AOC's announcement.

blindspot_narrative: The right is systematically avoiding anything suggesting friction inside Trump's legal/institutional apparatus (Scharf's appointment, Blanche's AG troubles), while the left is largely ignoring the mirror-image GOP fracture story (Tucker Carlson vs. 2028 mainstream) despite it being favorable to their framing. Both sides are underinvesting in the actual Iran/Strait of Hormuz foreign-policy substance, letting domestic primary drama dominate — meaning the most consequential geopolitical thread of the day is also the thinnest-sourced.
